function: p. 1-3: CSI feedback: a CNN autoencoder compresses downlink CSI eigenvectors into Q feedback bits at the UE and recovers them at the BS.
system: p. 2: Downlink MIMO, BS with Ntx=32 cross-polarized antennas, UE with Nrx=4, single stream, 12-13 subbands; 3.5 or 4 GHz, 10 MHz bandwidth (Table I); no RIS.
method: p. 3-4: CNN encoder-decoder (data arrangement, IB-Blocks with instance/batch normalization and SE attention, uniform quantization); supervised against true eigenvectors with loss 1-SGCS; 50 epochs.
data_channel: p. 2-3: Five public datasets, channel models CDL-A, CDL-C, UMa LoS, CDL-A, UMi (Table I); 32x4 cross-polarized antennas; 3.5 or 4 GHz; UE speed 3-30 km/h.
test_conditions: p. 4: Results reported per dataset (five datasets, 48 or 120 feedback bits); train/test split not described; no train-on-one, test-on-another case.
baselines: p. 4: Learned EVCsiNet [9] and PolarDenseNet [11] only; the 3GPP Type I/II codebooks are mentioned in the introduction (p. 1) but not compared.
metrics: p. 3-4: Mean SGCS (squared generalized cosine similarity) of recovered eigenvectors at 48 and 120 feedback bits; FLOPs and trainable parameters (Table III).
complexity: p. 4: Table III: DARENet (W=64, n=3) 114.8682 M FLOPs and 0.3854 M parameters versus EVCsiNet 3068.3546 M and 4.8300 M; PolarDenseNet comparison also given.
openness: p. 3: Datasets are public, link in footnote 1 (wirelessintelligence.com dataSet page); no code released.
q1_support: p. 2: Table I lists the channel models CDL-A, CDL-C, UMa (outdoor LoS), CDL-A, and UMi; p. 3 footnote 1 names the files "WLI_1_1023_CDLA300_3_52RB_omni_3GPP_R18AI.zip" (3GPP-named datasets).
q2_support: p. 4: "superior performance across all the datasets examined" is reported dataset by dataset (Table II); no statement trains on one dataset and tests on another, and the train/test split is never described.
q3_support: p. 4: "in comparison with the state-of-the-art benchmark, EVCsiNet" and PolarDenseNet are both learned; the codebooks appear only on p. 1 ("conventional codebook methods"), so no non-learned baseline is compared.
q4_support: p. 4: "DARENet requires fewer Floating-Point Operations (FLOPs) and has a smaller number of trainable parameters"; Table III gives 114.8682 M FLOPs and 0.3854 M parameters for DARENet (W=64, n=3).
q5_support: p. 1: "testing on 5 public datasets"; p. 3 footnote 1 gives the link "https://wirelessintelligence.com/#/dataSet?id=2c92185c7e3f1aa4017e3f2b9d6e0000" for datasets 1 to 5.
notes: Included, area 2: the learned function is CSI feedback (compression and recovery of eigenvectors). q1: Table I (p. 2) lists CDL-A, CDL-C, UMa, and UMi and the dataset files are named 3GPP (p. 3), but the paper never writes TR 38.901, so the reviewer may confirm that these are the 3GPP TR 38.901 models. q2: the five datasets differ in channel model, band, and speed, but each is reported separately; if the reviewer finds a train-on-one, test-on-another case, q2 would change. q3: only learned baselines are compared; the with and without data arrangement rows (Table IV, p. 5) are ablations. The bodies of Tables I to IV are read from the PDF page images, since the text extraction omits them.
